newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare gains on Sidek, certification.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare gains on Sidek, certification.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended slightly higher on Friday, after gains were almost wiped out by jitters over the Sidek group's finances and worries over pending certification of Mexico by Washington as a drug war ally.
"The certification row is still making people nervous and the Sidek business has compounded that," a Mexico City desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 2.79 points, or 0.07 percent, at 3,809.75. Trading volume was lackluster at 80.3 million shares.
Shares listed by the debt-ridden Sidek group and its subsidiaries fell sharply amid a flurry of adverse news to head the prominent decliners' list.
Both the New York Stock Exchange and the American Stock Exchange, meanwhile, halted trading in Sidek and its tourist arm Situr.

In Mexico, Sidek B shares fell 34 centavos (4 cents) to 48 centavos (6 cents), Situr B shares ended down 16 centavos (2 cents) at 22 centavos (3 cents), and steelmaking subsidiary Simec B shares slumped 54 centavos (7 cents) to 1.40 pesos (18 cents).

Situr posted a 1996 net loss of more than 3 billion pesos ($375 million) for the second year in a row in early trade, as a result of which parent company Sidek posted a 2.43 billion peso loss ($300 million).
Sidek announced it had posted negative stockholders' equity and any interested party could request liquidation under Mexican law.
Furthermore, the company said a new management team had uncovered "significant accounting and other irregularities" of the company's previous management.
The Sidek group has had considerable debt problems since an abrupt devaluation of the peso in December 1994.
On the broad market, 108 stocks were traded in total, of which decliners outnumbered gainers by 50 to 40.
Dealers said gains by telecommunications firm Telmex and corn flour and tortilla maker Maseca bolstered the market.
Traders said Telmex gained in parallel with its ADRs, up 1/2 to 39-1/2 on Wall Street, while Maseca recovered from a recent slide after being upgraded by Bear Stearns.
Telmex L shares ended up 16 centavos (2 cents) at 15.86 pesos ($2.01) while Maseca gained 10 centavos (1 cent) to 8.26 pesos ($1.03).
